brief: The merge pitch as a mechanism, not an agent's turn (Lean flow study, mechanisation). Today the orchestrator builds every train queue by hand: merge_train.py documents the queue schema in its docstring and nothing writes one, so a pitch happens only when an agent's turn assembles pull request numbers, verdict heads and comment ids. Every input is already machine-readable: the confirmed verdict on the verdict bus ref, the pull request's head, and tools/pr/app_approve.sh --carry, which decides whether a merge verdict on one head carries to another (only main merges whose tree equals merge-tree's result, or driver-file bot commits, and an identical branch diff). Add a queue builder to merge_train.py that writes the queue from the open non-record pull requests whose newest verdict is merge at the head or carries to it, oldest first, and leaves budget and policy paths to the serial route the batch admit already applies. Then run tools/audit/seat/queue_pre_flight.py, then train.sh with --bot-prs --approval-carry --pre-flight, once per pitch, from the tick loop, and never while a train's pidfile is live. Every merge goes through merge_pr.sh or the train, which approve (app_approve.sh, or tvofi's review under the mandate on a code-owned path) before merging; a posted merge verdict is not a GitHub approval. Controls: a fixture with one verdicted head, one carried head, one head the carry refuses, one blocked verdict and one budget file builds exactly the expected queue; an empty queue starts no train; a live pidfile starts none; mutants of each admission rule fail named arms. The first live pitch runs with the orchestrator watching.
